title: OpenAI publishes its internal pretraining perplexity numbers and Chief Scientist Jakub Pachocki proposes industry-wide common limits, gated on progress in understanding and monitoring AI behavior (Nov 22)
quote_verbatim: I believe frontier model developers should jointly endeavour to establish shared norms for how to evaluate such models and red-team safety cases for them
what_is_new: First lab disclosure of pretraining log-perplexity over time (GPT-3.5 ~0.99, GPT-4 ~0.91; a model at ~0.76 began producing breakthrough math results). The post says alignment and monitoring progress is unlikely to keep pace with the possible speed-up in pretraining, expects new capabilities at ~0.68-0.7, and proposes a first limit that developers would not cross until a monitoring milestone is reached (for example a successor to chain-of-thought monitors). Sam Altman ties it to the White House Accords; Microsoft AI reports a comparable number (item 004).
why_for_agiright: A frontier lab proposes measurable, shared pacing limits on its own capability progress: a concrete self-governance offer for the RSI and evaluation debate.
doubts: Main text read; footnotes and chart data partly read. The numbers come from OpenAI's internal code dataset, so other labs cannot compare without a shared eval set. Critics (e.g. @ziv_ravid, reposted by @GaryMarcus) call an unreproducible private benchmark a weak basis for a standard. @AndrewCurran_ notes the Accords are non-binding. Seen via @merettm (repost by @Miles_Brundage), @sama, @gdb, Techmeme 2124570014376407405. Topics index searched: perplexity (no match).

title: National Governors Association's bipartisan council issues AI principles (Nov 22): the federal government should handle national and international AI risks while states keep authority over AI use and consumer protection
author_or_publisher: National Governors Association (Governors Council to Secure American AI Dominance: Govs. Moore, Braun, Stein, Cox)
quote_verbatim: The federal government should address national and international risks as AI is developed, while states retain the flexibility to protect people
what_is_new: A bipartisan governors' position for the incoming Congress on federal-state roles (preemption debate): clear technical definitions, proportionate safeguards with regular review, less duplication; NGA Chair Moore says humans must stay in control.
why_for_agiright: The states' collective position on who governs frontier AI risk shapes any federal framework and preemption.
doubts: Bloomberg (via Techmeme) frames it as asking the US government to review AI models; the release says federal action on national and international risks and does not use the word review. Topics index searched: Governors Association (no match).

title: Amazon Threat Intelligence: a Chinese-nexus actor's Cairn AI agents found and exploited a zero-day in a medical-imaging app in about 11 minutes with minimal human direction
quote_verbatim: Amazon Threat Intelligence assesses with high confidence that it was a zero-day
what_is_new: An exposed, unauthenticated Cairn instance (found Sept 10) showed a ~48-hour campaign against East Asian universities: 16-hour and 6-hour autonomous attempts failed, but the agents found a path-traversal zero-day and got a root reverse shell; attribution to a Chinese-nexus actor is moderate confidence. Mustafa Suleyman says unsecured agent harnesses will probably need regulation next year.
why_for_agiright: A documented case of autonomous AI agents discovering and exploiting an unknown vulnerability in the wild.
doubts: Published Nov 20 (page metadata), before the window: marked stale. Earlier Cairn reporting is on the site (topic-2026-000342, NorForge; Gambit Security research cited by AWS). Topics index searched: Cairn, Amazon Threat (no AWS item).

title: Mustafa Suleyman: Microsoft AI "fully supports" OpenAI's transparency initiative and reports MAI-2 Base log-perplexity 0.819 on OpenAI's evaluation set
quote_verbatim: One of the hardest parts of AI safety is coordination, and this is a step in the right direction.
what_is_new: A second lab adopts the item 001 metric within a day: Microsoft AI commits to sharing pretraining progress on a common held-out set and reports its base model on OpenAI's dataset with OpenAI's permission.
why_for_agiright: Cross-lab uptake turns a single-lab proposal into a possible shared standard.
doubts: Post text cut off after the 0.819 figure; the linked Microsoft AI page was not found (microsoft.ai/news had no matching post). No other lab response found.
